title: Decision trees & random forests
summary: Trees recursively partition features; random forests average diverse trees trained on bootstrapped data.
why: Captures nonlinear rules while reducing the variance of a single deep tree.
interview: Compare impurity criteria and explain when bagging actually reduces variance.
derivation: A deep tree often has low training bias and high variance. Bootstrap sampling and random feature subsets diversify trees; averaging reduces the independent component of variance but shared correlation remains.
OOB estimates predict each training row using only trees whose bootstrap sample excluded it. sqrt(p) is a common classification feature-subset default, not a universal rule for every forest or task.

steps.note: About 36.8% of rows are absent from one large-N bootstrap sample.
steps.transformation: Draw N rows independently with replacement

steps.note: Choose a fresh subset at each split.
steps.transformation: Draw m candidate features per node

steps.note: Only excluded-row trees contribute to that row OOB prediction.
steps.transformation: Mean probabilities across trees; exclude in-bag trees for OOB

traps: Impurity-based feature importance can favor high-cardinality features.
Temporal data can make OOB estimates optimistic.
More trees do not eliminate correlated errors or label leakage.
tradeoff: Forests are robust tabular baselines but ensembles cost more memory and inference work than one tree.
code:
from collections import Counter
from math import log2

def impurity(labels):
    p = [n/len(labels) for n in Counter(labels).values()]
    return 1-sum(x*x for x in p), -sum(x*log2(x) for x in p)

gini, entropy = impurity([0,0,1,1])
assert gini == 0.5 and entropy == 1.0

explanations.title: Impurity reduction and stopping
paragraphs: A classification tree tests a feature threshold and partitions rows. For each candidate split compute parent impurity minus the sample-weighted child impurities. Gini is 1-sum p_c squared; entropy is -sum p_c*log2(p_c). Both are zero for a pure node.

For a balanced two-class parent, Gini is 0.5. Splitting into two equally sized pure children gives weighted child impurity zero and gain 0.5. A split that isolates one training outlier can also improve impurity, which is why depth and minimum leaf size matter.
A deep tree can have low training bias and high variance. Stopping rules or pruning trade fit for stability. Regression trees typically optimize squared-error reduction rather than class impurity.

explanations.title: Bagging and random features reduce correlated errors
paragraphs: Each tree receives a bootstrap sample drawn with replacement. At each split, only a random subset of features competes. Averaging or voting combines predictions. Random feature selection decorrelates trees that would otherwise repeatedly choose the same dominant predictor.

If T trees have individual variance sigma squared and pairwise correlation rho, the variance of their average is sigma squared times [rho+(1-rho)/T] under the equal-variance model. Adding trees shrinks the independent part but cannot remove shared correlated error.

sqrt(p) is a common classification feature-subset choice, not a universal setting for every forest. More features can strengthen individual trees while making them more correlated. Tune against held-out performance and cost.

explanations.title: Out-of-bag error and feature importance limits
paragraphs: A bootstrap sample of N draws excludes a row with probability (1-1/N)^N, approaching exp(-1), about 36.8 percent. Predict that row using only trees that excluded it to form an out-of-bag estimate.

OOB estimation still assumes the sampling design is appropriate. For temporal forecasting or correlated rows from one user, random bootstrap exclusion does not create a realistic future or unseen-user test. Use a suitable external split.

Impurity-based feature importance can favor features with many candidate split points. Permutation importance evaluates a different quantity and can be misleading with correlated substitutes. Neither establishes causality; inspect stability and known leakage features.
